lines: The citizenship interview. A hundred and twenty-eight civics questions.
The officer asks up to twenty. Get twelve right, and you pass.
This is Citizenship Study. Here's how to use it.

head: On iPhone,
Add to Home Screen.
lines: First, put it on your Home Screen. On iPhone, open the page in Safari.
Tap Share, then Add to Home Screen.

head: On Android,
Install the App.
lines: On Android, open it in Chrome. Tap the three dots, then Add to Home screen, or Install app.

head: Then Always
Open It From Here.
lines: From then on, open it from its icon. It works without internet.

head: Pick Your State.
Get Your Answers.
lines: Pick your state. Your senators, your governor and your state capital fill in.
Then type in your representative.

head: Study Cards.
Learn the Answers.
lines: Study cards teach you the answers. Pick a part, and tap the speaker to hear the question.
Tap Show answers to see every answer the officer accepts.
Tap Español for help in Spanish. The interview itself is in English.

head: Drill.
Practice Every Day.
lines: Drill is your daily practice. Say the answer out loud, then tap Show answers.
Be honest: I knew it, I guessed, or I missed it.
Guessed or missed, the question comes back sooner. Knew it, and it waits longer each time.

head: Mock Interview.
Like the Real Day.
lines: The mock interview is like the real day. The officer reads each question out loud.
Answer with the microphone, or type. Then tap Check my answer.
It stops at twelve right, or nine wrong, just like the real interview.

head: 65 or Older?
The 65/20 List.
lines: Sixty-five or older, with twenty years as a permanent resident? Tap the 65/20 list, and study only the twenty questions with a star.

head: Ten a Day.
Light Up the Mall.
lines: Your goal is ten questions a day. One missed day a week is a rest day.
On the National Mall, each landmark gets brighter as you learn its questions.
It turns gold when you knew them all on two different days.

head: Keep It Safe.
Save a Backup.
lines: Your progress is saved only on this phone. Tap Backup, save the file, and send it to yourself.
This app is not made by USCIS. Check the names of officials at uscis.gov before your interview.
Add it to your Home Screen, and study a little every day. Good luck!
